claims.text: Resistance of CrCoFeMnNi HEAs to simultaneous wear and corrosion is governed by their intrinsic ability to dynamically re-passivate.
Increasing Cr and Mo concentrations enhances rapid formation and regeneration of a protective oxide film during mechanical removal.
Rapid regeneration of the protective oxide film mitigates combined wear-corrosion degradation.
The baseline is a conventional CrCoFeMnNi HEA with lower concentrations of passivating elements than the modified alloy.
Increasing bulk Cr and Mo availability enables in situ formation and continual renewal of a passive oxide film.
The regenerated oxide film is adherent and protective.
Continual oxide-film regeneration minimizes local metal exposure and retards degradation while sliding intermittently removes surface layers.
The modified HEA will have lower material loss than the baseline under combined wear-corrosion testing.
The modified HEA will have lower corrosion current density than the baseline.
The modified HEA will develop shallower wear scars than the baseline.
The modified alloy's combined degradation rate will be lower than the sum of wear-only and corrosion-only degradation.
At moderate loads, passive-film regeneration will outpace mechanical film removal.
The conventional baseline has slower or less effective oxide-film reformation than the modified alloy.
The benefit of dynamic re-passivation will diminish or fail at sufficiently extreme wear conditions or loads.
The load threshold at which mechanical removal outpaces re-passivation is unknown.
The quantitative relationship between passivating-element concentration and oxide-film regeneration rate is unknown.
